classification.difficultyReason: Select explicitly taught opposite-angle/side/diagonal properties across six figures, combine a reflex-angle subtraction and solve three simple linear equations; all representations and targets are supplied.

content.prompt: Use the properties of a parallelogram to find the values of $x$, $y$, $z$, $\alpha$ and $\beta$ in the diagrams below. Give reasons.

spec.description: Parallelogram ABCD with AB extended to P, single parallel marks on AB and DC, double marks on AD and BC, and the original three angle labels.
spec.mathematics: Angle ADC is 110 degrees. Alpha is ABC and beta is CBP. A, B and P are collinear.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and unknown labels are visible.

answer.short:
$\alpha=110^\circ$, $\beta=70^\circ$.

Opposite angles are equal; angles on the straight line $ABP$ sum to $180^\circ$.
answer.worked:
$\alpha=110^\circ$ because opposite angles of parallelogram $ABCD$ are equal.

At $B$, angles on the straight line $ABP$ sum to $180^\circ$:
$$\begin{align*}\beta+110^\circ&=180^\circ\\\beta&=70^\circ.\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Parallelogram PQRS with red dashed intersecting diagonals and all four half-diagonal labels.
spec.mathematics: PQ is 12 cm and SR is x; PR halves are 8 cm and z; SQ halves are y and 6 cm. Opposite sides have matching parallel marks.
spec.answerVisibility: The intersection is unlabelled and no unknown values are supplied.

answer.short:
$x=12\text{ cm}$, $y=6\text{ cm}$, $z=8\text{ cm}$.

Opposite sides are equal and the diagonals bisect each other.
answer.worked:
$x=12\text{ cm}$ because opposite sides of parallelogram $PQRS$ are equal.

Its diagonals bisect each other, so $y=6\text{ cm}$ and $z=8\text{ cm}$.

spec.description: Three vertical parallel lines crossed by two parallel rising lines, preserving K–V labels, matching arrow families and the three angle sectors.
spec.mathematics: The angle below KL and to the right of KP at K is 100 degrees. Alpha is LQR; beta is above MN and to the right of the vertical at M.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the given 100-degree angle and unknown alpha and beta are visible.

answer.short:
$\alpha=80^\circ$, $\beta=80^\circ$.

Use opposite angles of parallelograms, a straight angle at $Q$ and vertically opposite angles at $M$.
answer.worked:
In parallelogram $KLQP$, $\angle PQL=100^\circ$ because opposite angles are equal. Since $P$, $Q$ and $R$ lie on a straight line:
$$\begin{align*}\alpha+100^\circ&=180^\circ\\\alpha&=80^\circ.\end{align*}$$
In parallelogram $LMRQ$, $\angle LMR=\alpha=80^\circ$ because opposite angles are equal. Hence $\beta=80^\circ$ by vertically opposite angles at $M$.

spec.description: Two adjoining parallelograms share SV. The 30-degree leader identifies STU, and a large arc below V marks the exterior reflex angle WVU.
spec.mathematics: RSVW and STUV are parallelograms; WRS is 50 degrees and STU is 30 degrees. RW, SV and TU share triple parallel marks; RS and WV share single marks; ST and VU share double marks.
spec.answerVisibility: The reflex angle is labelled beta without its value; interior component angles at V are not supplied.

answer.short:
$\beta=280^\circ$.

The two interior angles at $V$ are $50^\circ$ and $30^\circ$; subtract their sum from $360^\circ$.
answer.worked:
$\angle WVS=50^\circ$ because opposite angles of parallelogram $RSVW$ are equal.

$\angle SVU=30^\circ$ because opposite angles of parallelogram $STUV$ are equal.

Angles at $V$ sum to $360^\circ$:
$$\begin{align*}\beta&=360^\circ-50^\circ-30^\circ\\\beta&=280^\circ.\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Parallelogram GDEF with G left, D top, E right and F bottom; adjacent angles labelled alpha and 3 alpha.
spec.mathematics: GD is parallel to FE and DE is parallel to GF. Alpha and 3 alpha are adjacent interior angles.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the original unknown angle expressions are shown.

answer.short:
$\alpha=45^\circ$.

Co-interior angles between $GD\parallel FE$ are supplementary.
answer.worked:
Since $GD\parallel FE$, co-interior angles on transversal $GF$ are supplementary:
$$\begin{align*}\alpha+3\alpha&=180^\circ\\4\alpha&=180^\circ\\\alpha&=45^\circ.\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Parallelogram MJKL with two solid diagonals and an unlabelled intersection; all original algebraic segment and side labels are retained.
spec.mathematics: MK halves are x and 2x−5; JL halves are y and 7−y. JK is 4 and ML is 18−2z. MJ and LK share double parallel marks; JK and ML share single marks.
spec.answerVisibility: Only given expressions are visible, with no solved values or added intersection name.

answer.short:
$x=5$, $y=3.5$, $z=7$.

The diagonals bisect each other and opposite sides are equal.
answer.worked:
The diagonals of parallelogram $JKLM$ bisect each other:
$$\begin{align*}x&=2x-5\\0&=x-5\\x&=5.\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}y&=7-y\\2y&=7\\y&=3.5.\end{align*}$$
Opposite sides of $JKLM$ are equal:
$$\begin{align*}18-2z&=4\\18&=4+2z\\14&=2z\\z&=7.\end{align*}$$
